newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: Life was breathed into South African industrial shares shortly before the close of trade on Tuesday after stocks had held in weaker territory for the best part of the day after falls on Wall Street on Monday night.

Dealers said expectations of a stronger Dow Jones index on Tuesday swept the local market following the release of a lower than forecast rise in the fourth quarter U.S. employment cost index -- an indicator closely watched by the Federal Reserve.

Industrials almost stole the limelight from gold shares which after a day of strong gains on the back of a more robust bullion price, slipped off their best levels as the metal once again edged below the $356 an ounce level.
However, the gold index ended firmly in the red, up 3.93 percent or 54.1 points to 1,429.4.
The March gold futures contract held firm and was last quoted at 990/1,008 from 969 settlement on Monday.
"Bullion might have slipped back after the figures in the U.S. proved anti-inflationary," one dealer said.
Bullion is often regarded as a safe investment haven against inflationary pressures.

Dealers said earlier that after weeks of subdued and anxious trade as the gold price weakened, the local gold stock market was jumping at the chance to make gains following bullion's brief rise above the $357 level on Tuesday.
The metal hit a 3-1/4 year low on January 23 when it touched $346 an ounce.
Marginal mines, which are most vulnerable to movements in the gold price, were taking heart from the strength with Freegold putting on 210 cents to 34.10 rand -- a rise of over 6.5 percent.
Amongst other gold stocks and mining houses Anglo rose 450 cents to 252.50 rand, Dries upped 180 cents to 44.40 rand and Vaal Reefs jumped 16 rand to 322 rand.
Meanwhile on the industrial board dealers were optimistic about gains on Wednesday.
"It looks like we will run tomorrow opening up some 35-40 points better if the Dow is higher tonight," a trader said. "Industrials already moved better today on the back of the American data."

Factors pointed to a stronger Wall Street opening were the U.S. S&P 500 Index Futures March contract moving higher and the key 30-year long bond surging to 6.87 percent shortly after the release of the employment data.
Dealers said a more buoyant rand, which tested a two-month best level of 4.56 on Tuesday, and a stronger bond market were also seen helping industrial stocks on Wednesday.
The industrial 100 percent index ended 25.1 points firmer at 8,069.0 with the related March futures contract rising in late trade to last be quoted at 7,876/90 from 7,857.
Amongst industrial shares SAB lifted 125 cents to 124 rand, Richemont rose 200 cents to 65 rand and Sun International put on 10 cents to 285 cents.
Gains on both industrial and gold boards boosted the overall market index by 47.0 points to 6,736.0.
